newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end firm after auction, tan book.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end firm after auction, tan book.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended slightly higher, resuming gains after a mild set-back on 10-year note auction results.
U.S. Treasury sold $12.0 billion 10-year notes at an average 6.205 pct yield. The bid-to-cover ratio was 2.24 and non-competitive bids totalled $380.9 million.

Shortly after the auction results, the Fed's beige book of regional economic activity showed the U.S. economy grew moderately in June/July, with growth in some areas more brisk. It said the U.S labor market tightened, but cited only scattered wage pressures.
September Treasury bond futures cut gains and then waffled on both sides of Tuesday's close after the auction and beige book, but soon resumed the morning uptrend.

"The Fed's tan book did not show any real insight," a Eurodollar trader said. "I just think that unless there's some real negative news out there the market is going to continue to grind higher," he said.
But traders said gains would likely be tentative until the last leg of Treasury's $38.0 billion quarterly refunding is digested.
Treasury will sell 30-year bonds on Thursday.
Also on Thursday are the latest weekly jobless claims, June wholesale inventories and June consumer credit.
Traders pegged support in September T-bonds at 114-12/32 and 114-4/32. Resistance was seen at 115-00.

At the close, September T-bonds were up 5/32 to 114-24/32, notes rose 3/32 to 109-25/32, munis rose 4/32 to 120-17/32, Eurodollars rose 0.010 to 94.085. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
